title: Cognitive Dissonance
shortDefinition: The mental discomfort experienced when your actions, beliefs, or values clash with one another.
dailyExample: Knowing smoking or staying up until 2 AM is bad for your health, but telling yourself 'I had a stressful day, so I deserve this' to reduce internal tension.
psychologyTheory: First coined by Leon Festinger in 1957. The human brain cannot tolerate contradictory beliefs without distress, so it instinctively invents rationalizations to restore harmony.
inTherapy: In counselling, identifying dissonance helps clients recognize when excuses are covering up grief, fear of failure, or unresolved conflict.
practicalTakeaway: When you catch yourself offering ten elaborate justifications for a simple habit, pause and ask: What uncomfortable feeling am I trying to avoid facing?
